title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten named Philadelphia places with direct evidence of free, no-purchase access.

cards.title: See the Liberty Bell
cards.subtitle: 6th and Market Streets, Independence National Historical Park
cards.notes: Enter first-come, first-served, pass through screening, then move through the self-guided exhibits before seeing the bell.
cards.short_summary: A free, ticketless historic exhibit centered on the original Liberty Bell.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that admission is free and no tickets are required for the Liberty Bell Center.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; security screening is required and entry is first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Explore the President's House Site
cards.subtitle: 6th and Market Streets, Independence National Historical Park
cards.notes: Walk the outdoor exhibit at your own pace and use its panels, videos, and visible foundations to discuss freedom and enslavement.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided outdoor exhibit interpreting the Washington household and enslaved people who lived there.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that the outdoor President's House Site is free and requires no tickets.
cards.source_title: Visiting the President's House Site: From Enslavement to Emancipation
cards.access_notes: Open daily, year-round, 7 a.m.–10 p.m.; outdoor exhibit entered from Market or 6th Street.

cards.title: Step into Old City Hall
cards.subtitle: 5th and Chestnut Streets, Independence National Historical Park
cards.notes: Use the north Chestnut Street entrance and look into the restored Supreme Court chamber before continuing through the historic district.
cards.short_summary: A free first-come, first-served visit to an 18th-century Supreme Court chamber.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists free admission and no ticket requirement for Old City Hall's Supreme Court chamber.
cards.access_notes: The Supreme Court Chamber is open daily 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; entry is first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Browse the Merchants' Exchange exhibit
cards.subtitle: Walnut and 3rd Streets, Independence National Historical Park
cards.notes: Stop into the lobby exhibit to examine the building's role in Philadelphia's nineteenth-century financial and postal history.
cards.short_summary: A free lobby exhibit inside a landmark designed by William Strickland.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists the Merchants' Exchange Building lobby exhibit as free and ticketless.
cards.access_notes: Lobby exhibit is open Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; the building is wheelchair accessible.

cards.title: Watch printing at Franklin Court
cards.subtitle: Franklin Court, between 3rd and 4th Streets
cards.notes: Visit the public viewing area to see the eighteenth-century-style printing operation, then explore the surrounding Franklin Court passageway.
cards.short_summary: A free historic printing stop within Independence National Historical Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies the Franklin Court Printing Office among sites requiring no tickets and no fee.
cards.access_notes: Confirm daily building operations before going; the NPS identifies a designated public viewing area in the Printing Office.

cards.title: Meet at the LOVE Sculpture
cards.subtitle: LOVE Park, 16th Street and JFK Boulevard
cards.notes: Use the surrounding walking paths and seating for a photo stop or an easy meetup before heading along the Benjamin Franklin Parkway.
cards.short_summary: A public-art gathering point in John F. Kennedy Plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Philadelphia identifies the LOVE Sculpture as free to visit at LOVE Park.
cards.source_title: 40+ Free Things to Do in Greater Philadelphia
cards.access_notes: The sculpture is in the outdoor public space of LOVE Park; park amenities and nearby vendors may charge separately.

cards.title: Use Dilworth Park's public space
cards.subtitle: 1 S. 15th Street, beside Philadelphia City Hall
cards.notes: Bring a friend to sit under the tree groves, walk through the plaza, or check the calendar for a free lawn screening or performance.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor City Hall plaza with no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Philadelphia states that there is no cost of admission to visit Dilworth Park.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space; skating, food, and other programmed amenities can have separate charges.

cards.title: Walk The Rail Park
cards.subtitle: 1300 Noble Street entrance; also Callowhill Street between 11th and 12th
cards.notes: Enter at Noble Street for the accessible slope, then take a slow loop past benches, plantings, industrial artwork, and the Story Wall.
cards.short_summary: A free elevated park built on former Reading Railroad tracks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rail Park's official site states that Phase One is free and open daily.
cards.access_notes: Phase One is free and open daily; use the Noble Street entrance for wheelchair-accessible access.

cards.title: Lounge at Spruce Street Harbor Park
cards.subtitle: Penn's Landing waterfront
cards.notes: Use the seating, lights, floating gardens, and hammocks for a waterfront meetup; skip the optional concessions and paid activities.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal public waterfront park with free entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Philadelphia states that Spruce Street Harbor Park is free and open to the public through September, with concessions and select activities separate.
cards.source_title: Spruce Street Harbor Park: 5 New & Surprising Things to Do for 2026
cards.access_notes: Seasonal and free through September; concessions and select activities are pay-as-you-go.

cards.title: Climb the Rocky Steps
cards.subtitle: Philadelphia Museum of Art, 2600 Benjamin Franklin Parkway
cards.notes: Take the outdoor staircase at your own pace, pause at the top for the skyline view, and keep the visit outside the museum's ticketed galleries.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor stair climb and skyline-view stop at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Philadelphia identifies the Rocky Steps as free and says visitors can run the steps or visit the Rocky Statue without museum admission.
cards.source_title: 40+ Free Things to Do in Greater Philadelphia
cards.access_notes: This card covers the exterior steps only; entry to the Philadelphia Museum of Art galleries is separate.
